svg.title: The read path for one query_database call, including both failure branches
svg.desc: A seven stage pipeline drawn as a snake, left to right along the top and right to left along the bottom, with each stage outlined in the color of whoever owns it: blue for the client, terracotta for the server, green for PostgreSQL. A strip of six chips above the pipeline names the checks in the order they run: one statement, root is a query, no nested mutation, no SELECT INTO, no blocked function, and LIMIT then clamp. A dashed line drops from that strip into stage two. The stages are: a tools/call for query_database arriving; validation, which is pure and touches no pool; regeneration of the statement from the parse tree, which becomes the executed_sql field; acquiring a connection from the read-only pool as role mcp_readonly; executing the fetch, where the statement timeout applies; coercing values so that NUMERIC becomes a string; and returning a QueryResult published as structured content. A vertical dashed line runs down the figure between regeneration and acquisition, labelled nothing is acquired until here, and the only arrows that cross it are the ones into and out of the database. Two dashed red branches leave the main line. The first leaves validation and reaches a box saying the call was refused before anything was acquired, carrying ok false and an empty executed_sql on a response whose result type is still complete with isError false, which is a value the model can correct. The second leaves execution and reaches a box where PostgreSQL itself refused, with permission denied and canceling statement due to statement timeout. A note beside it says the second branch is the interesting one, because it is the read-only role and the statement timeout doing the job the validator only approximates, and it is the layer that still holds when the validator is wrong.
svg.text: Nothing is acquired from a pool until every check has passed. Two exits, and the second is the one that matters.
resultType complete, isError false. A value the model can correct.
canceling statement due to statement timeout
The second branch is the interesting one.
It is the read-only role and the statement timeout doing
the job the validator in stage 2 only approximates, and
it is the layer that still holds when stage 2 is wrong.
Outlines: blue is the client, terracotta the server, green PostgreSQL.
